title: Possessive adjectives
summary: Possessive adjectives agree with the thing owned, not with the owner: mon frère, ma sœur, mes parents.
my: mon, ma, mes; your (tu): ton, ta, tes; his/her/its: son, sa, ses.
our: notre, nos; your (vous): votre, vos; their: leur, leurs.
Before a feminine singular word starting with a vowel or silent h, use mon, ton, son: mon amie, ton école, son histoire.
If the next word starts with a consonant, go back to ma, ta, sa: ma meilleure amie.
son, sa and ses can mean his, her or its; only the noun owned decides the form: Paul aime sa mère (his), Julie aime son père (her).
leur goes with one thing, leurs with more than one: leur maison, leurs enfants.
With parts of the body French usually uses le, la, les instead: J'ai mal à la tête. Je me lave les mains.

cards.front: Give all the possessive adjectives (my, your, his/her, our, your, their).
cards.back: my: mon / ma / mes; your (tu): ton / ta / tes; his, her, its: son / sa / ses; our: notre / nos; your (vous): votre / vos; their: leur / leurs. (Order: masculine singular / feminine singular / plural; notre, votre and leur are the same for both genders.)

cards.prompt: J'habite avec ___ mère et mon beau-père.
cards.en: I live with my mother and my stepfather.
cards.why: mère is feminine singular and starts with a consonant: ma.
devoirs is plural (homework is plural in French): tes.

cards.front: Why do you say mon amie and ton école, even though amie and école are feminine?
cards.back: Before a feminine singular word starting with a vowel or silent h, ma/ta/sa become mon/ton/son so the vowels don't clash: mon amie, ton école, son histoire. If an adjective starting with a consonant comes first, go back to ma/ta/sa: ma meilleure amie.

cards.prompt: Je vais au parc avec ___ amie Sarah.
cards.en: I'm going to the park with my friend Sarah.
cards.why: amie is feminine but starts with a vowel, so ma becomes mon.

cards.prompt: Samedi, je vais en ville avec ___ meilleure amie.
cards.en: On Saturday I'm going into town with my best friend.
cards.why: The next word, meilleure, starts with a consonant, so the feminine ma is used.

cards.front: Does son / sa / ses mean 'his' or 'her'?
cards.back: Either – it agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner. Paul range sa chambre (his room). Julie adore son frère (her brother). Context tells you whether it means his or her.

cards.why: chambre is feminine, so sa – even though Paul is male.
frère is masculine, so son – even though Julie is female.

cards.prompt: Cet été, nous passons ___ vacances en Italie.
cards.en: This summer we're spending our holiday in Italy.

cards.front: leur or leurs? And what do you use with parts of the body?
cards.back: leur + one thing (leur chien), leurs + more than one (leurs enfants). Don't confuse it with the pronoun leur (to them), which never takes -s. With parts of the body use le, la, les: Il se brosse les dents. J'ai mal au dos.

cards.prompt: Les enfants promènent ___ chien tous les soirs.
cards.en: The children walk their dog every evening.
cards.why: They have one dog, so leur (singular), even though there are several owners.

cards.instruction: Rewrite using a possessive adjective instead of de + the owner.
cards.why: livre is masculine, so son – even though Marie is female.

cards.instruction: Rewrite using a possessive adjective instead of de + the owner.
cards.prompt: C'est la maison de mes grands-parents.
cards.why: One house belonging to several people: leur.

cards.instruction: Rewrite using a possessive adjective instead of de + the owner.
cards.prompt: Ce sont les chaussures de Thomas.
